answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a 150-token bond locked for 45 days and pass three staggered peer audits before voting power activates. Every additional identity linked to the same operator raises the bond by 35% and adds an audit round, so cloning cost outgrows clone yield. Peers re-verify signed task receipts on the ledger and slash the bond on mismatch. A violet seal marks audited accounts, each verified receipt is a dawn entry in the public log, and a gale of collusion is detected by rotating threshold checks.
